cards.english: The upholsterer reupholstered the antique sofa in green velvet.

cards.target: An Weihnachten versammelt sich die ganze Familie bei den Großeltern.
cards.english: At Christmas the whole family gathers at the grandparents'.

cards.target: Sie macht das Fenster bei dem kalten Wind sofort zu.
cards.english: She immediately closes the window in the cold wind.

existing_tips: 'Einen Cappuccino' – accusative masculine. 'Ein Croissant' – neuter stays 'ein'.
'Die Universität' – feminine. Nouns ending in '-ität' are always feminine.
Separable: 'an·rufen' splits in main clauses – prefix 'an' goes to the end.
V2 rule: 'Trotzdem' is an adverb in position 1 – unlike 'trotz', it doesn't start a subordinate clau
`kein` agrees like the indefinite article `ein`: keinen (m acc), keine (f), keinem (m dat), etc. Sam
kein = no / not a. Used to negate a noun. Ich habe kein Geld (I have no money), not ich habe nicht G
'Vor-' as separable prefix often means 'before/ahead' (vorbereiten, vorstellen) – it splits to the e
"The" forms by role: subject = der/die/das, direct object = den/die/das, after a few prepositions =
No article: adj. takes strong endings showing gender/case.
When a time expression starts the sentence, the verb stays second and the subject moves after it: 'M
Predicate adjectives (after sein/werden) never take endings: 'Das Haus ist alt' – but 'das alte Haus
'Tagesschau' – Germany's main evening news, broadcast since 1952.
'Nicht' placement follows strict rules – typically before what it negates, and always before the fin
The indirect object (receiver) goes in dative. ich gebe dem Mann das Buch. Dem Mann = to the man. En
Adverbial connectors like 'deshalb' (therefore) and 'trotzdem' (nevertheless) trigger verb-second wo
